dedupe_keys.name: socio technical infrastructure interdependencies and urban sustainability transitions netherlands interdependency matrix and coding data

description: This dataset holds the research material behind a qualitative study of how interdependencies between infrastructure systems enable or restrict urban sustainability transitions, based on examples from the Netherlands. It distinguishes seven socio-technical interdependency types (functional, evolutionary, spatial, life-cycle, policy or procedural, market, and culture or norm) and contains the document selection, interview design, a description of the Dutch urban sustainability transition, the coding tree, a list of infrastructure systems, a list of multi-mode interactions and an infrastructure interdependency matrix in Excel, together with project documents such as the City-Zen and 't Ven cases. It was compiled by Cem Gürsan and Vincent de Gooyert of the Faculty of Management Sciences at Radboud University. Version 6 of June 2023 is accessible on Mendeley Data as free downloads (Word, Excel, PDF and PNG files) under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the material is qualitative and case-based, the matrix records coded relationships, not measured flows, and third-party documents may need separate permission. It supports the design of interdependency structures and scenario narratives for cross-sector infrastructure models in cities; a related record is NISMOD.
